# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Wellpoint Maryland — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Sawyer Foster
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-08
**Member:** Sawyer Foster
**Member ID:** W356952515
**Reference number:** POC-65BD57974D-81336
**Service denied:** Shoulder labral / instability repair, CPT 29806
**Governing policy:** *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal – Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1)*, https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PDF-Joint-Surgery-2025-11-15.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my shoulder labral/instability repair (CPT 29806). The notice dated 2026-08-08 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Wellpoint Maryland to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure, because the records in my chart address each of the criteria the plan itself publishes in the guideline named above. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Because the denial is based on incomplete documentation rather than a clinical disagreement, I am setting out below what the plan's own criteria require and where the corresponding information appears in my records. If any document did not reach the reviewer, I am glad to have it resubmitted right away.

## The plan's criteria and my records

The guideline states:

> "Capsulorrhaphy is considered medically necessary when ALL the following criteria are met:"

I understand that this sentence introduces a list, and that the excerpts available to me may not reproduce every condition in that list. I ask the plan to identify in writing each specific criterion it found unmet or undocumented. Taking the criteria I do have, item by item:

**1. "History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation"**
My records document 14 months of recurrent episodes of shoulder instability with apprehension, and three anterior dislocations since my symptoms began. The most recent dislocation was reduced in the emergency department.

**2. "Shoulder pain and/or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living"**
My records document that I avoid overhead reaching and that I cannot return to my work lifting.

**3. "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift)"**
My examination documents positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift, with full strength. These are the same maneuvers the policy names.

**4. "MRI demonstrates at least ONE of the following:"** — including **"A labral lesion consistent with the clinical instability"**
My MR arthrogram of the shoulder dated 2026-06-11 shows an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, and an intact rotator cuff. The anteroinferior labral tear corresponds directly to the anterior instability found on my examination and to my three anterior dislocations.

**5. "Failure of at least 12 weeks of conservative management (unless history of traumatic dislocation and multiple dislocations during management)*"**
I completed supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification from 2026-03-29 to 2026-06-21 — 12 weeks, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

**6. "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."**
In addition to the supervised physical therapy above, my records document NSAIDs taken for 4 months during flares and activity modification. My records note that an injection was not indicated for instability.

**7. "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"**
The 12-week supervised course described above was completed for this episode and is documented in the discharge note.

**8. "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"**
After that course of therapy, my examination remains positive for apprehension, relocation, and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift, and I continue to avoid overhead reaching and remain unable to return to my work lifting.

**9. "More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"**
Surgical repair is exactly what is now under consideration, which is why this prior authorization request was submitted.

## The imaging documentation requirement

The guideline states:

> "Imaging report. The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months. In the absence of a detailed report, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

and

> "For advanced imaging (CT, MRI, ultrasound, bone scan), there must be a report from a radiologist that correlates with clinical findings. In the absence of such a report, the summary findings from the radiology report should be included in the clinical records."

My MR arthrogram was obtained on 2026-06-11, which is within 12 months of both the request and this appeal. The summary findings from that study — anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion), small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, intact rotator cuff — are in my clinical records, and they correlate with the instability findings on my physical exam. The policy contemplates exactly this situation and permits the summary findings in the clinical records where a separate report is not in hand.

The guideline also states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My compliance is documented: 24 completed visits over the 12-week course, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.

## What I am requesting

1. That Wellpoint Maryland overturn the 2026-08-08 denial and approve CPT 29806.
2. In the alternative, that the plan tell me in writing which specific criterion from *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal – Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1)* it found undocumented, and which document it was expecting, so that my surgeon's office can send that exact item without further delay.
3. That the plan confirm it received and reviewed my MR arthrogram findings of 2026-06-11 and my physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-03-29 to 2026-06-21.

I am also requesting a free copy of the complete criteria the plan applied to this request, and copies of all records the reviewer relied on.

Per the denial notice, my appeal must be received within 180 days of 2026-08-08, that is, by **2027-02-04**. I am sending this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also submit or check on my appeal by logging in at anthem.com or through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card. Anthem (Elevance) plans are state- and plan-specific, so I am using the appeal address on my denial letter as the authoritative one.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. My shoulder has dislocated three times, therapy has been completed as prescribed, and my surgeon has documented that this repair is needed. Please contact me at [my phone number] if anything further is required.

Sincerely,

**Sawyer Foster**
Member ID: W356952515
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [List of documents enclosed — e.g., MR arthrogram report of 2026-06-11; physical therapy discharge note; office notes from Dr. Okafor; copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-08]

**cc:** Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery
